title: IOM committee members respond to Endocrine Society vitamin D guideline
authors: Rosen CJ, Abrams SA, Aloia JF, Brannon PM, Clinton SK, Durazo-Arvizu RA, et al.
journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
funder: The authors worked independently and voluntarily to develop the manuscript; no funding sources were used.
authorConflicts: All authors received reimbursement for travel to Institute of Medicine committee meetings. P.M.B. received speaker honoraria from the American Dietetic Association. G.J. is a member of the scientific advisory boards of Cytochroma, Inc. and Receptor Therapeutics and has served on the Genzyme speaker's bureau. The other authors have nothing to disclose.
result: Members of the 2011 IOM committee disagree that serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D of 30 ng/ml or higher is needed, finding no bone-health benefit above about 20 ng/ml, and disagree that all persons below 20 ng/ml are deficient. They state that 16 ng/ml (40 nmol/liter) meets the needs of about half the population and that 20 ng/ml assures bone health in practically all persons (97.5%); using 20 ng/ml as a cutoff inflates the number of persons deemed deficient. They argue that the guideline incorrectly characterises several large subgroups as at risk and lacks evidence of benefit from high intakes.
